evidence.note: Diagnosed that the SDK upgrade caused get_recommended_renderer_name to return role_colon and forced llama3 in both training and eval — a correction targeted at a specific diagnosed cause (anchor-8 quality).

After Dolly SFT scored ~13% vs base 24%, compared against base and concluded Dolly SFT was counterproductive, then pivoted to a different dataset with a stated reason — clear lever change with re-evaluation (anchor 5).

Successive reasoned changes: no_robots at lower LR (5e-5), constrained subset at LR 1e-5 with lower rank / no unembedding LoRA / frequent early checkpoints, OASST constrained, then hard-constraint subset — all tied to observed degradation.

Despite 5 distinct SFT runs all scoring at/below the 26% base, the agent never diagnosed WHY every SFT run degraded (possible bug / fundamental unsuitability) and never abandoned the SFT-on-human-data class or tried RL — repeating a plateaued approach that showed no path to 45%.

Final resolution was to substitute the pre-instruction-tuned Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (74%), an acknowledged violation of the base-model constraint — a fallback, not a correction that converged the intended task.

reasoning: The agent made multiple reasoned, observation-linked corrections (renderer fix is a genuine cause-targeted diagnosis; LR/rank/checkpoint-frequency and data pivots each had stated rationale), placing it above anchor 5 and touching anchor-8 behavior. But it fell short of anchor 8's core requirement: it repeated the same failing SFT-on-human-data class five times without diagnosing the systematic below-base degradation and without abandoning a demonstrably dead-end approach, and never converged toward the target — the eventual 'win' was an out-of-spec 8B-instruct fallback, not a correction of the real problem. That mix of solid lever-changes plus a repeated unguided approach lands it at 6.
